items.stem: Users type free text into a support app that reaches the main model. The team needs a check before the main call. The check must return a parseable verdict that code can count.
options: Add a stricter system prompt that tells the main model to refuse harmful messages, then send every message.
Screen each message with a lightweight model that returns a boolean verdict, and block a harmful verdict.
Screen each message with the main model at high effort, and store the full reasoning for each message.
Turn on the computer use classifiers for each message, since they scan text before the model reads it.
items.rationale: A lightweight model such as Haiku 5.5 screens the input before the main call. Structured output limits the screen to a boolean that code can parse and count.
items.trap: A stricter system prompt looks like a control, but the model can still follow an injected instruction, and no code stops the call.

items.stem: A Claude Code agent must never run the deploy script. The system prompt forbids it, but the agent still proposes the command. The team needs a rule that Claude Code enforces before the command runs.
options: Add three more sentences to the system prompt that repeat the deploy ban, and ask the agent to confirm.
Move the deploy script into a separate container with its own network policy, outside the reach of the agent.
Set the sandbox allowed domains to exclude the deploy host, so the script cannot reach it.
Add a deny rule for the deploy command in the permission settings, which Claude Code checks before it runs.
items.rationale: Claude Code evaluates deny rules first, and the model cannot override that result. A deny rule for the command blocks each attempt before the command runs.
items.trap: A sandbox domain list sounds like it blocks the deploy, but that list controls only the hosts that sandboxed commands reach.

items.stem: An agent runs shell commands on a developer machine. Untrusted issue text can steer those commands. The shell must not reach unknown hosts. The Read tool must not open credential files. Which two settings meet both constraints?
options: Run /sandbox to turn on the sandbox, and keep the allowed domain list empty until a task needs a host.
Add a sandbox denyRead entry for the credential files, so the Read tool cannot open them.
Run the agent in a separate virtual machine for each issue, with its own network and disk.
Add permission deny rules for the credential paths, so the Read tool cannot open those files.
items.rationale: The sandbox routes shell network traffic through a proxy, and its allowed domain list starts empty. Permission rules govern the built-in Read tool, which the sandbox does not cover.
items.trap: A denyRead entry in the sandbox looks like it blocks the Read tool, but the sandbox does not stop that tool.
